findings.title: Green recovery tests omit both unsafe outer-worker evidence gaps
findings.trigger: The implementation regresses by treating the post-spawn pre-claim pid-null window or a live PID with an unsupported or unreadable bound identity as stopped.
findings.impact: The focused suite still reports 89 of 89 passing even though cancel can publish a safe terminal and release the writer fence while a real worker remains alive.
findings.evidence: The reused-PID test covers a supported Linux identity with a deliberately different value, and the worker-claim test covers a spec-digest mismatch. Neither exercises pid null after spawn, a live PID with an unknown identity type, an unavailable current identity, or exact identity readback. Independent direct fixtures reproduced cancelled, lock deletion, and fence_count 0 in the missing-identity cases.
findings.suggestion: Add deterministic RED cases for post-spawn pid null and live-but-unavailable or unsupported identity, asserting status unknown and that cancel signals first but creates no cancelled result, removes no lock, and releases no fence. Add a focused worker-claim readback case for changed or omitted identity without a production test backdoor.

coverage_refs: node --test tests/delegate.test.cjs tests/acp-driver.test.cjs tests/acp-conformance.test.cjs: 89 passed, 0 failed
positive_observations: The suite now reaches real fault seams and covers missing inner-writer evidence, conflicting recovery facts, symlink-safe cancellation, fence overlap, and frozen outcome_unknown behavior.
The exact three-file command is deterministic and passed independently outside the writer session.
limitations: A green aggregate count is insufficient until the newly reproduced outer-worker cases become executable regressions.
